newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto's son defends Indonesia's car policy.
newsitem.headline: Suharto's son defends Indonesia's car policy.

text.p: President Suharto's youngest son, who heads the only company that benefits from Indonesia's national car policy, defended the controversial programme on Thursday, saying it was necessary for the country.

Hutomo Mandala Putra, the head of PT Timor Putra Nasional, said in a statement he was optimistic Indonesia could successfully argue in favour of its national car policy at the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"The Indonesian government had many good reasons for issuing this policy," Mandala Putra said, adding that foreign car manufacturers, which dominate the local market, had never proposed transfer of technology programmes to help develop Indonesia's domestic industry.
"If Indonesia cannot build its own car...it will lose an opportunity. And besides that it will remain dependent on other countries for its imports," he said.

PT Timor Putra National was given preferential tax and tariff breaks by the government in February this year to manufacture Indonesia's first national car in partnership with Kia Motors of South Korea.

Japan, the United States and the European Union have all taken the issue to the WTO, arguing that the policy discriminates against existing automobile joint ventures in the country. Most of them are with Japanese firms.

Although PT Timor Putra Nasional must reach a local component level of 60 percent within three years of starting production, the first batch of cars, which went on sale earlier this month, are fully built and assembled in South Korea.
PT Timor Putra Nasional has said it plans to start assembly in Indonesia by March next year before commencing full manufacturing in 1998.
